  meeting is being broadcast via teleconference. Members of the public may participate in-person in the
  Council Chambers, or virtually in the meeting in the following ways:

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1 669 900 6833) from any phone,

  speak using the call in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails

  - Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &

  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 839 2736 1481, Meeting Password: 339794. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JUNE 14, 2022

1.  ALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZERUNYAN at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall and remotely via
teleconference, in accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361) and City Council Resolution
Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493, 2498, 2499, 2503, 2505 and 2507 due to the continuing state of
emergency, including masking and social distancing directives as a result of the threat of the
COVID-19 virus.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG
Led by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF

3.  ROLL CALL
City Council Members Present:  Zuckerman, Stegura, Schmitz, Huff, Zerunyan

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Assistant Carol Corea

4.  CEREMONIAL

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING JUNE 2022 “PRIDE MONTH”

MAYOR ZERUNYAN expressed the importance of recognizing equality and declared June
2022 “Pride Month” and presented a proclamation. He introduced Lisa Augustine, resident of
Rolling Hills Estates.

Lisa Augustine thanked the City for their support and commended the City on being a safe city;
recognizing “Pride Month” shows that the City is one of acceptance and inclusiveness.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA stated that recognizing “Pride Month” is especially important
this year since the City adopted Diversity, Equity and Inclusion statement. She thanked Ms.
Augustine for her attendance and activism.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, TO
  APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-D AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING
  ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES: Zuckerman, Stegura, Schmitz, Huff, Zerunyan

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF JUNE 2022

8.  NEW BUSINESS
A.  MCGOWAN CONSULTING LLC, PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT (PSA)
  FOR MS4 PERMIT CONSULTING SERVICES FOR THREE FISCAL YEARS (2022-
  25)

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve a three-year Professional Services
  Agreement with McGowan Consulting LLC for MS4 Permit compliance assistance for
  FYs 2022-25 in the not-to-exceed grand total amount of $346,429 ($109,890 in FY
  2022-23), all to the satisfaction of the City Attorney.

Director Wahba provided a summary of the staff report (as per the staff report).

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ inquired if there is a point when the City will meet MS4 Permit
compliance. Director Wahba explained that the Torrance Airport project that was just approved
is designed to divert stormwater to the sanitary sewer. He stated that the proposed Drywell
Siting Project will divert stormwater to an infiltration basin. These various projects take time,
but they are in progress.

In response to a question by COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA, City Manager Grammer stated
that the city has been working Kathleen McGowan for more than 20 years on stormwater permit
compliance issues.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF asked about the Public Participation Guidelines referenced in the
Task Order. Kathleen McGowan responded that all of the activities the city is involved with are
reported on an annual basis. She further explained that the permit that became effective in
September 2021 requires that specific metrics on engagement are tracked. She also provided
examples of their outreach efforts including educating on illicit discharge into the storm drain.

Ms. McGowan stated that the Torrance Airport and Drywell Siting project are both working
towards capturing the 1-inch of rainfall, which is the minimum to bring the city in compliance;
this would move the city into only having to do baseline maintenance, and consulting costs
would be reduced.

In response to a question by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, Ms. McGowan responded that she
and Director Wahba attend the Peninsula Watershed Management Group (WMG) meetings,
which are helpful to coordinate efforts with the other cities.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE A THREE-YEAR PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH
  MCGOWAN CONSULTING LLC FOR MS4 PERMIT COMPLIANCE

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JUNE 14, 2022
   ASSISTANCE FOR FYS 2022-25 IN THE NOT-TO-EXCEED GRAND TOTAL
  AMOUNT OF $346,429 ($109,890 IN FY 2022-23), ALL TO THE
  SATISFACTION OF THE CITY ATTORNEY

  AYES:  Zuckerman, Stegura, Schmitz, Huff, Zerunyan

B.  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT (PSA) TO RETAIN GEOSYNTEC
  CONSULTANTS INC. TO CONDUCT A DRY WELL SITING STUDY

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve a Professional Services
  Agreement (PSA) with Geosyntec Consultants, Inc. to conduct a Dry Well Siting
  Study in the amount of $169,883, all to the satisfaction of the City Attorney.

Director Wahba provided a summary of the staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA referenced an attachment to the proposed contract where
Geosyntec notes a confluence of drainage points with a point in Rancho Palos Verdes, and
states that if an agreement could be reached the drywell siting would be done there. She asked
if this would be a cost savings to the overall project. Ms. McGowan clarified that this would not
be part of this project and stated that the scope of this study is to look at siting the wells in the
city.

Chris Wessel, Geosyntec, stated that it may provide cost saving, but other factors such as
long-term maintenance would need to be considered; this was included since it came up as
part of their initial analysis.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF asked about community engagement and disruptions to the
community due to noise and activities related to this project. Mr. Wessel explained that, at this
stage, there will be minimal noise and it would be for less than a day. He further explained that
the community engagement portion is in part driven by the MS4 Permit and with Measure W
and stated that this is a driving factor in any future funding applications. He added that
community engagement is important to keep residents informed and provide an opportunity to
ask questions and provide input. Director Wahba added that staff will be notifying the HOAs
and immediate neighbors about activities related to this project.

Ms. McGowan added that the potential for an area in Rancho Palos Verdes only applies to the
portion that is going to the Harbor; the drywell that is needed to comply with is going to
Machado Lake and would not be shared with Rancho Palos Verdes.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT (PSA) WITH
  GEOSYNTEC CONSULTANTS, INC. TO CONDUCT A DRY WELL SITING
  STUDY IN THE AMOUNT OF $169,883, ALL TO THE SATISFACTION OF THE
  CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Zuckerman, Stegura, Schmitz, Huff, Zerunyan

C.  PROJECT LIST FOR SB1 FUND ELIGIBILITY (RESOLUTION NO. 2508)

  Recommendation: That the City Council Approve Resolution No. 2508, adopting
  a list of projects for Fiscal Year 2022-23 funded by SB 1, the Road Repair and
  Accountability Act of 2017.

Director Wahba provided a summary of the staff report (as per the agenda material).

MAYOR ZERUNYAN asked if the streetscapes would still be done this summer. Director
Wahba confirmed that this is still the plan and the contract should be presented at the next
City Council meeting.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JUNE 14, 2022
   APPROVE RESOLUTION NO. 2508, ADOPTING A LIST OF PROJECTS FOR
  FISCAL YEAR 2022-23 FUNDED BY SB 1, THE ROAD REPAIR AND
  ACCOUNTABILITY ACT OF 2017.

  AYES:  Zuckerman, Stegura, Schmitz, Huff, Zerunyan

9.  OLD BUSINESS
A.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 741 AMENDING AND
  RESTATING MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 17.60 (SIGNS)

  Recommendation: That the City Council (1) conduct the second reading of
  Ordinance No. 741; and (2) adopt Ordinance No. 741

Director Wahba stated that there have been no comments or changes since the first reading
and introduction.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE TO CONDUCT THE SECOND READING OF ORDINANCE NO.
  741 AND ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 741

  AYES:  Zuckerman, Stegura, Schmitz, Huff, Zerunyan

B.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER (VERBAL
  REPORT)

City Manager Grammer reported that the number of COVID cases and hospitalizations have
fluctuated and are currently trending upward; staff will be monitoring whether changes are
made to the Health Officer Order . The County is currently in a “medium level” of transmission,
as defined by the CDC. City Manager Grammer also reported that earlier this week, the CDC
announced that they would not be requiring pre-departure COVID testing for those entering
the United States from international travel.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS
NONE

11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE

12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF reported that South Bay Cities Council of Governments (SBCCOG)
will be transitioning officers on June 23, 2022. El Segundo Mayor Drew Boyles will be ending
his term. Staff will be preparing a certificate to present to him. Rancho Palos Verdes’ Council
Member, John Cruikshank, is scheduled to be the next Chair.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF also reported that on Thursday, June 23, 2022, the Palos Verdes
Peninsula Chamber of Commerce will be hosting a presentation by Dr. Christopher Thornberg,
Vice President of Beacon Economics, who will be providing an annual economic forecast
follow-up entitled, “The Post Covid World: Will the Sweet turn Sour.”
COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ thanked the Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber of Commerce
for a successful street fair, which she and her family attended.

13.  MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL ITEMS

NONE

At 7:56 p.m. MAYOR ZERUNYAN adjourned the meeting in memory of Dandi O’Connor.
MAYOR ZERUNYAN and COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA expressed their sympathies to her
family.

The meeting was adjourned to the next regular City Council meeting, which will be held on
Tuesday, June 28, 2022 at 7:00 p.m.
